claims.statement: `electron . --accept` is dispatched before any single-instance logic in the main entry, so the acceptance battery neither takes nor needs the lock and can run beside a resident panel; the mode installs an empty `window-all-closed` handler and requires `accept/battery.js` inside the same Electron app context, and `npm run accept` runs the build first so the controller and every panel it spawns share one `dist`.

The battery is a controller, not a panel: `launchPanel()` spawns `process.execPath` with `['.']` (the default guard entry, which hides native icons and then spawns the panel) and `DECK_EVENT_LOG` pointing at the evidence JSONL, so the panel's real pid is taken from its own `boot` evidence record rather than from `child.pid`, and `stopPanel()` escalates from killing the child to `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F`.

Because the event file and the panel DOM survive restarts, every post-restart assertion carries a time lower bound (`sinceMs`, `lastBootMs()`, or a wall-clock start) and hotzone rectangles are re-read from a `hotzones` record of the current generation; `waitStable()` exists because dock ranking is recomputed asynchronously about a second after boot, so first-painted rectangles can point at items that have since moved.

Transparency is proven against a backdrop the battery supplies itself: a frameless controller-owned `BrowserWindow` loading an 80 px conic checkerboard is pushed to `HWND_BOTTOM` under the panel, sample points that survive a `WindowFromPoint` filter are counted, and PASS needs at least 500 valid points with more than 90 % checker-colour hits (tolerance 30), with one ESC-then-re-shoot retry for `TOPMOST` shell flyouts.

The same transparency screenshot carries a solid-text assertion: more than 30 near-white pixels inside the clock card's rectangle must be found, which is meaningful because the opacity slider only moves the card background alpha while text colours stay literal.

Default pass-through is asserted from both the window style and real input: the extended style must contain `WS_EX_TRANSPARENT | WS_EX_LAYERED`, a left click at an empty DIP point must turn the foreground into a desktop class, and a right click must surface the desktop context menu (including the Win11 WASDK host class `XamlExplorerHost…`).

Hotzone routing is asserted with a real ordinary window as the control: entry into the clock-card hotzone must clear `WS_EX_TRANSPARENT`, a click there must not raise the panel or steal foreground (still below the control, `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE` intact) while still delivering `clock-card-clicked`, leaving must restore transparent, and the panel must remain below the control in the top-down window enumeration.

Carried desktop items are verified against an independent scan: a PowerShell enumeration of the user desktop plus `CommonDesktopDirectory` (Hidden/System filtered, UTF-8 forced) must equal the panel's reported item set with same-named common items shadowed by user items, and native icons must be invisible (`SysListView32` fact, re-implemented in the harness) while the panel runs.

Two shortcut fixtures cover the icon path: the battery creates lnks to different executables (`notepad.exe`, `System32\charmap.exe`), builds an in-process kernel from `dist/main/kernel.js` with all timers disabled and isolated layout-store and usage directories, and requires `desktop/icon` to return different `data:image/…` data URLs for them — a regression to the byte-identical generic `.lnk` icon fails here.

A double-click launch probe is asserted behaviourally: a uniquely named shortcut whose target writes a marker file must appear in the 1 Hz rescan, produce `desktop-launched` with `ok: true` after two clicks inside `GetDoubleClickTime`, and its target must write the marker file within 10 s; deleting the shortcut must remove the item from the render.

The icon-hide crash path is exercised by force: `taskkill /F` on the panel pid must be followed by native desktop icons becoming visible again within 6 s together with an `icons-restored` record whose reason is `panel-exit` and the guard's exit, after which the battery launches a fresh panel generation with an explicit time lower bound so the old `boot` record cannot be reused.

Arrangement assertions are behavioural: the seeded pinned item must occupy `dock[0]` with `source: 'pinned'` and no other entry may be pinned; new `.docx`/`.pdf` files must group as `office`/`pdf` and disappear when deleted; a real `SendInput` drag must yield `desktop-moved` with `ok: true`, a reordered `desktop-rendered`, and the same order after a panel restart; and the settings overlay's reset must clear all `placed` entries while keeping the pinned one first.

The search section is gated on the environment: it first proves Listary is live with its own HTTP client against `127.0.0.1:<port>/api/v1/search` (a freshly created probe file must rank first, 90 s budget) and returns early after a failure if that pre-check does not pass, so no UI assertion in the section can be reported green without a working engine.

The search UI chain asserts activation through a hotzone click plus a hard foreground gate (three attempts, foreground must belong to the panel pid), `keyboard-mode-on` with the panel still below every normal window, pasted `Ctrl+V` input producing `search-results-rendered`, `Enter` opening a window whose title contains the probe token, `Ctrl+Enter` producing a `CabinetWClass` window, `↑`/`↓` selection as `search-selection-moved index: 2`, `ESC` and desktop-click deactivation with reasons `esc` and `blur`, and the engine-offline badge reproduced through a dead loopback port written into `config.json`.

The settings overlay is asserted end to end: opening via the `settings-btn` hotzone must record `settings-opened` (with the slider rectangle and current value) and put `settings-card` into the hotzones while raising `keyboard-mode-on` with the panel as foreground; the initial slider value must equal `config.appearance.cardOpacity`, and a real slider drag must keep the renderer input, the kernel set, the applied value and the persisted config within 1 % of each other.

Closing and persistence of the settings overlay are asserted separately: `ESC` must record `settings-closed` with reason `esc` plus `keyboard-mode-off` and the return of `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE`, clicking the clock card must record reason `blur`, and after a drag plus a panel restart a boot-time `settings-opacity-applied` within 1 % of the persisted config must appear.

The `config.panel` geometry phase overwrites `config.json` with a fixed rectangle, archives the event file to `03-runtime-events-preP6.jsonl` and deletes it so the next `boot` is unambiguous, then requires the relaunched window to match DIP × scale factor within 24 physical pixels; this cut is why the final `03-runtime-events.jsonl` covers only the post-P6 portion of a run.

Single-instance admission is asserted observably: a second `electron .` launch must exit with code 0 in under 3 s, the event log must contain `single-instance-refused`, and the original panel window must still exist with an unchanged count of `Chrome_WidgetWin_1` top-level windows.

Tray registration is checked against the registry fact source rather than the app: `HKCU:\Control Panel\NotifyIconSettings` must contain an entry whose `ExecutablePath` equals `process.execPath`, and visibility is checked by promoting the entry (`IsPromoted = 1`, previous value remembered for restore) and locating the amber `#f5a623` icon in the `Shell_TrayWnd` strip by connected-cluster analysis, with a panel restart and an 8 s rescan when nothing is found and a hit count above the pre-run baseline required for PASS.

The tray exit is closed through the shared teardown path: `Win+B` plus a UIA focus walk must find a focused tray element whose name contains `AGENT DECK`, and a posted `WM_CLOSE` must end in the panel pid dying within 10 s, a `quit` record from `before-quit`, and the amber count returning to the baseline — while the human right-click menu itself stays a manual check because injected context menus do not reach Electron tray icons on Win11 26200.

The Win+D phase requires its control window to be found minimised before any conclusion is drawn, expects the panel to be exempt (it is a `WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW`/`skipTaskbar` window) while recording the panel's own `wind-minimized` as the alternative, and then drives `SW_MINIMIZE` to assert `wind-minimized` with `IsIconic` true, `wind-restored` about 1.5 s later, the original rectangle within 24 px, and the restored control window again covering the panel (re-pin effective).

Session-row direct access is tested with a substitute process and a seeded session because the real tools must not be disturbed: `config.tools.qoder` is repointed at `charmap.exe`, a probe session is written under `~/.qoder-cn/projects/DECK-PROBE-09/` with a fresh mtime so it enters the active pool, probe windows are identified by the executable that owns them rather than by class name, and the section self-skips instead of touching user processes when the probe program is already running.

The session-row section asserts three distinct outcomes with diagnostics: a click on a session row must return `action: 'launched'` with a new window owned by the probe executable when the tool is not running, `action: 'focused'` with the same window restored and its pid in the foreground when it is, and `action: 'degraded'` with `ok: false` when the mapping is blanked — after which a clock-card click must still succeed, proving the panel survived. It also performs the feature's one read-only check that every explicitly configured `config.tools.*.launch` target exists on the machine, and it is placed second to last because it restarts the panel with a patched config.

The plugin phase proves the built-in cards go through the plugin contract: each of `clock`, `weather`, `sessions`, `hardware` must have a `plugin-mounted` record and a `*-card` hotzone in the current generation, the `clock-card` rectangle must equal the battery's `CARD_DIP` constant, and the retired Qoder status card must be absent while `sessions-card` occupies top 152 / height 522.

Hot-plug is asserted without a restart and without trusting a self-report: copying `samples/hello-plugin` into `<userData>/plugins/hello` must yield `plugin-mounted hello`, `hello-mounted` (the module actually ran) and a `hello-card` hotzone; editing `card.js` must re-mount it; removing the directory must drop the card from the hotzones; re-adding it must bring it back — with the count of `boot` records unchanged across all four steps.

Verdict and exit-code semantics: `Report` writes one timestamped `PASS`/`FAIL`/`NOTE` line per assertion into `app/accept/evidence/<name>.log.txt` and ends with a verdict line carrying the pass and fail counts; the process exits 0 on pass, 1 on any failure, and 2 on an unhandled crash — an exception thrown inside `main()` is recorded as a failure instead, so it yields exit 1.

Runtime events are the machine-readable half of the evidence: `DECK_EVENT_LOG` turns each spawned main process into a JSONL recorder appending `{t, type, …}` lines through `fileEventLog`, the battery filters those records by type and time to gate assertions, and it truncates the file at run start so the first `boot` is unambiguous.

Screenshots are DPI-correct physical-pixel captures: `capture(rect, name)` invokes `lib/capture.ps1`, which declares `SetProcessDPIAware()` before `CopyFromScreen`, and all pixel analysis is done by re-reading those PNGs through Electron's `nativeImage.toBitmap()` (BGRA).

The battery keeps its own DIP copy of the renderer's layout geometry (`CARD_DIP`, `LEFT_CARDS_DIP`, `RIGHT_CARDS_DIP`, `SEARCH_CARD_DIP`, `DOC_ZONE_RIGHT_DIP`, `DOCK_STRIP_DIP`) and computes every click and screenshot rectangle as `panelRect + round(DIP × scaleFactor)`, so a card moved in `index.html` without the matching constant turns probes into clicks on pass-through space or assertions over the wrong pixels; the only runtime cross-check is the plugin phase's exact comparison of the `clock-card` hotzone rectangle with `CARD_DIP`, and `SEARCH_CARD_DIP` is declared but never read.

The battery mutates machine state and must put it back: teardown restores the promoted tray registry value, the battery's own Notepad window, the search probe directory once its handle is released, `layout.json` (restored from backup or deleted when it did not exist), the windows minimised by `clearDesktop`, and the saved cursor, and it falls back to `electron . --icon-restore` when a forced kill left the icons hidden although they were visible before the run.

Interrupting a run is operationally hazardous: the battery rewrites `app/config.json` several times (panel geometry, a dead search port, a probe tool mapping), seeds `layout.json` in the real `userData`, writes the tray's `IsPromoted` value, minimises every non-topmost ordinary window and creates desktop fixtures, and a Ctrl+C or taskkill skips the `finally` blocks that undo it — leaving a patched config, a seeded layout store or hidden desktop icons behind.

Several acceptance items are explicitly not automated: visual alignment is reviewed by a human from the screenshots (the built-in-card assertion says so in its own PASS text), no battery assertion covers the Startup autostart entry so a genuine reboot check stays manual, and weather depends on the network so a fetch failure is downgraded to a note.

Occlusion degrades the harness rather than the product, and the recorded run demonstrates it: the checked-in `03-battery.log.txt` ends with `VERDICT: FAIL (pass=79 fail=2)`, whose two failures are a probe-fixture timeout (the probe shortcut's target never wrote its marker file) and the read-only tools-mapping check reporting that `config.tools.kimicode`'s launch target is missing on that machine, while earlier rounds were attributed to a Chromium window covering the sampling band and another raising itself over the desktop.

Evidence is written into the repository working tree at `app/accept/evidence/`, which `.gitignore` does not exclude (it ignores `app/node_modules/`, `app/dist/` and `app/config.json`), so a battery run shows up as working-tree changes beside the recorded reference round whose screenshots, verdict log and event files other pages cite.
